key_insight: HSVDQuant turns low-rank-assisted 4-bit PTQ into a coupled optimization problem, using a deflated Hessian and activation-noise modeling to preserve accuracy with much smaller rank.
engineering_relevance: It enables faster, lower-cost W4A4 quantization for diffusion transformers and even improves downstream LLM accuracy at rank-4 versus much larger low-rank baselines.
method: Decompose weights into a low-bit residual plus a high-precision low-rank branch.
Eliminate the output-side low-rank factor to form a deflated Hessian that avoids re-learning errors already captured by the rank term.
Add an activation-noise surrogate so the solver explicitly accounts for 4-bit activation quantization error.
evidence_signal: Across five diffusion backbones, rank-4 HSVDQuant beats rank-4 SVDQuant on PSNR and LPIPS, and on Qwen3-8B it raises MMLU from 61.50% to 68.17% while often outperforming rank-32 SVDQuant with up to 6.25x faster quantization.
watch_item: The method is solver- and calibration-dependent, so real-world gains may vary with backbone, calibration data quality, and implementation of the Hessian/activation approximations.
paper_title: Deflating the Hessian: Rank-4 W4A4 Quantization for Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
